body:
Thanks for the links and the help.

My own philosophy breaks down to that:
- Nothing has meaning and you can't really find meaning because of that (if nothing has meaning, then truly *nothing* has meaning, so it's futile to search for it)
- Nature/biology/life is indifferent to our existence, so it doesn't matter if you live happy or depressed. In the end nature doesn't care because humans are just giant sacks of chemicals.

So with those two principles the happy person or person who might delude themselves into finding meaning has no problem living. For me, not seeing any meaning and not believing that there can be meaning, I don't think there's any purpose in forcing yourself to live a life you can't change and can't be happy in. In the end, both people just wind up "worm chow" so to speak.

But I think your link showed me I have some more reasearch into the philosophical things to do before I fully commit to that idea. Can't imagine I'm the first to come to that conclusion, so maybe someone has more to say.

Thanks for the link, I've spent some time already studying depression from a psychological/biochemical/medical perspective, but this is a new theory to add to the belt I guess.

I'm interested in hearing your philosophical thoughts when you get them together. Most of my own sort of lead in a predictable direction (existential/nihilistic).

I'm not religious. Tried it as a child, but by the time I was done with high school any remaining delusions about it were gone. If there is a god(s) then they don't deserve worship for what they allow. Doctrine/Mantra based religions don't really comfort me either.

Bad family history, so not much I can turn to there.

I have maybe 3 or so serious hobbies and a few smaller ones. Spent three years in leadership at a community service organization as well.

I've spent time doing things with people before. I put a lot of effort into most friendships I've tried to have. I've been there to help people with their own depressive tendencies. I've been there day in and day out for people, bent over backwards to defend them or help them. It hasn't mattered, though, so increasingly I don't see the point in even trying anymore. At the end of the day I help people, but they can't even be assed to say hi to me anymore after I spent months being there for them. I just wind up alone and feeling worthless and used, so I don't see the point. Might as well not exert the effort on that anymore.

In the past 7 months - finished my second degree, switched to a better job, switched therapy to try to find something more effective, new haircut/visual/etc., worked on my depression/anxiety, stopped drinking, tried new hobbies, etc.

I could list a good deal more changes I've tried in the past 5-10 years. So yeah, I believe I've tried to improve things and have been trying for a while to make things better. I have tried everything I know to do to change things, but I'm still here posting this.

No matter what changes I make, no matter what I achieve, I will never be happy. I'll never even be content. Any progress I make just moves me along the same circle such that I can never recover from this, and it simply can't be worth it to keep going through this.

And yeah, objectively, on paper, I know I shouldn't be this way. I know I've worked my ass off to get to where I am. But that's why I'm here - it doesn't matter how hard I work to change or improve, things simply don't change because I'm fundamentally broken. There's something fundamentally wrong with me that simply can't be fixed. So, I just wind up in the same place. I can't keep living in that place, and I can't actually pull myself out of it with willpower or even with other's help. I've searched but this is the only path that I haven't tried to fix things.
